items.statement: Submitting a RESET bdev I/O clears its cached I/O path, starts bdev_nvme_reset, and returns without generic completion handling.
Each controller reset is dispatched to the app thread, where the handler selects a reset function, records the completion callback, and invokes that function.
When reset-function selection returns EBUSY, the reset I/O is appended to pending_resets and the handler returns.
When reset-function selection returns EALREADY for a disabled controller, the handler normalizes the result to success before continuing.
A negative reset-selection result other than EALREADY is passed unchanged to reset continuation.
Reset startup freezes each bdev channel by setting its resetting state to true.
When rc is zero, bio->cpl.cdw0 is cleared to zero.
Reset continuation is posted to the reset I/O's owning thread.
Controller completion removes each retained I/O from the head of pending_resets and resumes it with the controller result.
Reset completion aborts queued retry I/Os and clears resetting while unfreezing each bdev channel.
Among negative reset-selection results, only EALREADY is normalized to success; every other negative value remains an error passed to reset continuation.
When a second reset is submitted from another thread while the first controller reset is active, the second bdev I/O becomes the first entry in pending_resets.
When a failed controller reset has no alternate trid ready for immediate retry, completion resumes every queued reset with a failure result.
Controller removal during an active reset causes both the active reset I/O and the concurrently submitted reset I/O to complete as failed.
Controller reset completion repeatedly removes the head of pending_resets and resumes that bdev I/O with the controller-reset outcome.
items.description: Reset completion repeatedly removes the first pending reset from the controller queue and resumes it with the controller-reset result.
